Order No. 04/Dated: 15 April, 2024
 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Jasidih P.S. Case No. 90 of 2023, instituted under
Sections 341, 323, 504, 506, 498A, 34 of the I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, the
petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.
As per the FIR, the allegation against the petitioner is that the marriage of the complainant was solemnized with this petitioner five years ago as per Hindu rites and customs.

After 2-3 years later,
the petitioner demanded of gold ornaments, furniture, etc. as additional dowry and on non-fulfilment of this, they abused and physically assaulted her.
It is further alleged that petitioner has ousted her from the matrimonial home, after keeping the child.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all whatsoever alleged in the FIR.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has further submitted that both the parties have settled their dispute before the DLSA, Deoghar.

Hence,
petitioner may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
Learned APP appearing for the State assisted by learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 have not controverted the aforesaid submission made on behalf of the petitioner.

It appears that in terms of order dated 15.03.2024 that the matter was referred to DLSA,
Deoghar and in course of mediation, both parties have agreed to settle their dispute. Mediation

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation against petitioner coupled with materials available on record, I am inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Twenty thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned A.C.J.M., Deoghar in connection with Jasidih P.S. Case No. 90 of 2023 subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and also with further direction that both the parties shall appear before the concerned trial court on 25.04.2024 and on that, the petitioner shall furnish bail bond and the petitioner, in compliance of terms and conditions of the settlement arrived at DLSA, Deoghar, took his wife / opposite party no.
2 at her matrimonial home.
(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Sachin-Simran/ Page 2|2 Bikas Pandit @ Bikash Pandit vs The State Of Jharkhand on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48623222/
